answer.rationale: The declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the funnel itself, and two inherited records (memory_86, memory_31) independently support onboarding/signup simplification as a lever on exactly those metrics. That makes it the best fit for the single slot: it addresses the internal deterioration rather than only reacting to the competitor's price move. I am spending verification on memory_73 and memory_86 rather than on the memories I am least sure about generally, because those two carry the most decision weight. memory_73 (promotional pricing) is the obvious pull given the competitor's entry pricing, and it is also the memory whose consolidated summary is most likely to have shed caveats: 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' is a top-of-funnel claim that says nothing about retention, discount-cohort LTV, or margin, and discount-acquired SMB accounts are a classic source of revenue that looks qualified for a quarter and then churns. Before I decline that direction I want the original record, and if it turns out the pricing test actually tracked retained revenue and held up, that changes my ranking. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the basis for my intended action and its summary is stated in adoption terms ('completion rates', 'time-to-value', 'early product adoption') with no evidence about downstream qualified revenue. Note the tension with memory_44: enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows, which means stripping fields or steps out of onboarding could degrade the routing and qualification signal that sends enterprise-shaped accounts to demo-request. A lift in self-serve completion that quietly starves the enterprise pipeline would be a net loss against a sustainable-qualified-revenue objective. So the downstream risk here is real even for my preferred option, not just for pricing. Caveats I am holding rather than resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries with archived sources, so absent verification I treat their effect sizes as directional only; memory_31 (day 12) and memory_86 (day 52) may be the same underlying finding counted twice, which would make my apparent two-source support illusory; the day-12 'durable lift' claim is the oldest record and predates whatever changed this quarter, so the mechanism may simply no longer hold. I therefore run this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout, with segment-preserving guardrails: keep the enterprise/demo-request path intact, and measure retained qualified revenue and pipeline quality alongside completion and activation rather than declaring success on funnel metrics alone. If verification shows memory_86 measured only completion, or that it duplicates memory_31, I would downgrade to a small guarded test or reconsider activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger 6% decline through in-product nudges without altering the data captured at signup.
